newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU declines comment on Guinness/GrandMet merger.
newsitem.headline: EU declines comment on Guinness/GrandMet merger.

text.p: The European Commission declined to comment on Monday on whether it would probe the 20-billion pound ($32.5 billion) merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan Plc saying the companies had not yet submitted the plan for clearance.
"I've not seen anything," a source close to European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert told reporters.

The source said the companies had not sounded out the Commission for its opinon before agreeing the merger, as large companies tended to do. But that was no indication of whether they would formally notify the deal or indeed whether it required EU regulatory approval.
The two companies said on Monday they did not expect any regulatory problems as the joint spirits business would give the group less than 10 percent of the world's accessible spirits market.
The merger will create the world's seventh largest food and drinks company, GMG Brands.

The Commission must vet all mergers and acquisitions involving companies with a combined global turnover of at least five billion European currency units and EU sales of 250 million ecus each. Corporate concentrations must be submitted to the Commission shortly after being announced.
